name: Khartoum International Airport
before:
Sudan's main airport, and one that needs checking before anything is quoted into Khartoum.

The airport was closed for almost two years, from 15 April 2023 to 25 March 2025, during the Battle of Khartoum in the Sudanese civil war. On the first day of the war the Rapid Support Forces attacked the airport, reportedly firing on an arriving Saudia airliner, and two civilians were killed in separate incidents on the site. Around 20 aircraft are believed to have been destroyed in the fighting, after which the RSF occupied the airport. Treat any schedule as provisional and verify it directly.

A replacement is planned. The New Khartoum International Airport is to be built at Omdourman 40 km from the centre, with two 4,000 metre runways, an 86,000 square metre terminal and a 300 room hotel, built by China Harbour Engineering.

The airport began as the Royal Air Force field Gordon's Tree, which housed an RAF squadron from 1940 and an operational training unit from 1942. The last RAF unit left in July 1956, months after Sudanese independence.

It also hosts a Sudanese Air Force transport squadron and the Police Air Wing.
after:
The airport for Sudan's capital, and one that needs checking before anything is quoted into Khartoum.

It closed when Sudan's war began on 15 April 2023, and it was among the first places the Rapid Support Forces attacked. Domestic flights resumed on 22 October 2025, and the first international flight since the war, a Kuwait Airways service, landed on 28 April 2026. The airport was hit by drones again on 4 May 2026.

Treat any schedule as provisional and verify it directly with the airline before booking.

claims.note: Was 'Sudan's main airport'. During the war Port Sudan became the country's international hub (Xinhua, Feb 2026), so main is not safe to say.
